title: First Ever “Black Hole Star” Discovered at the Dawn of Time
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyFirst Ever “Black Hole Star” Discovered at the Dawn of TimeBlack hole sun, now it’s comeJCBy Jake Currie12:00 PM CDT on August 12, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleRecently, astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) to peer deep into the history of the universe noticed something strange—a very bright, very red dot. Now, the team behind its discovery has published their analysis of the cosmic oddity in Nature, and it’s unlike anything ever seen before.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 102.2K 00Milky Way's Enormous Black HoleShareNextStayAccording to the international team of astronomers, the bright red dot appears to be a combination of a massive black hole and a star, around the size of our entire solar system. The team arrived at that conclusion after modeling a variety of scenarios to explain the object’s peculiar characteristics. Typically, redness in a celestial object is a telltale sign of cosmic dust, similar to how wildfire smoke turns the sunset red, researchers say. But other signatures from the object didn’t match up with the dust hypothesis. The astronomers also didn’t detect any heavy metals usually produced by mature stars—only the simple elements hydrogen and helium. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
